title: How computers and the internet work
purpose: Explain how computers represent numbers, text, images and sound in binary; how logic gates, processors, memory and storage work; how software and files work; how the internet moves data with packets, IP addresses, DNS and HTTP; and how encryption and good habits keep you safe.
primary_reading: Khan Academy: Computers and the Internet

weeks.3: Text, images and sound as numbers
weeks.6: Inside the computer: processor, memory and storage
weeks.8: Files and how data is stored
weeks.9: Networks and the internet: packets and IP addresses
weeks.10: The web: DNS, HTTP and browsers
weeks.12: Privacy, safety and computing in society

blocks.deliverable: Convert ten numbers between binary, decimal and hexadecimal.
Compress a short message with run-length encoding.
Build the truth table of a half adder.
Week 7 midterm; explain what happens when you open a file.
Trace a web request step by step.
Write a short guide to strong passwords and spotting phishing.
Submit the project; take an unseen 45 minute final in week 14.

project: Explainer: make an illustrated guide (poster, slides or booklet) that follows one photo from the camera to a friend's screen: how it becomes bits, is compressed, travels in packets across the internet, and is shown as pixels.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
